fun_fact: The summer of 2026 has left much of Europe parched — the Rhine, Danube, and Po have fallen to near-record low levels, exposing dry riverbeds and cracked earth. When these rivers and the lakes they feed run low, everything downstream takes a hit: farms lose irrigation, hydropower and power-plant cooling falter, cargo barges run aground, and lakeside tourism dries up. See Europe's scorched rivers and lakes [here](https://www.theguardian.com/world/gallery/2026/aug/07/europe-dry-riverbeds-scorched-earth-hot-weather-in-pictures).
